headline: No shared execution or data channels: prompt-injection, leakage, and capability-conflict risks are effectively blocked by both docs-only, non-runnable content agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent exposes a shared communication channel or ingest path by default. Agent A is docs-only content-writing with network egress none; agent B is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP. Without a bridge, prompt injection cannot propagate between them.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared clipboard, file, or MCP bridge, reassess as non-none.
IF an orchestrator starts piping A's text directly into B's prompt, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared clipboard and filesystem bridges.
Do not pipe A's raw output into B without sanitization.
Verify the orchestrator does not add hidden prompt prefixes.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no data classes touched, no filesystem read/write, and no network egress. Agent A is docs-only and agent B is documentation-only, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to move from one agent to the other or out to a third party.
conditions: IF either agent is given files, secrets, or PHI to process, reassess leakage risk.
IF network egress is enabled on either agent, leakage risk changes materially.
mitigations: Keep secrets and regulated data out of both agents.
Confirm network egress remains disabled.
Confirm no files are mounted into either runtime.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if data-bearing inputs are later introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface to conflict over. Agent A has no documented filesystem or git write capability, and agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. With no shared mutable resource, capability conflict is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory, reassess conflict risk.
IF a shared git repo is introduced with write permissions, conflict risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
Do not grant git write permissions to either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is later enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is not documented because neither agent is runnable in a way that would let one agent's output drive the other's actions. Agent A is content-writing and docs-only; agent B is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout or action-taking tools, so B cannot operationalize A's output.
conditions: IF B is wrapped in an external workflow that treats A's text as authoritative, reassess.
IF either agent is connected to downstream action tools, cascading error becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not use A's output as an authoritative source without review.
Keep B in documentation-only mode.
Avoid attaching action-taking tools to either agent.
requires-engineering: add verification gates if a workflow later chains outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes are touched, and both agents show no network egress or secret handling. Because the profiles do not indicate residency, retention, or regulated-data processing, there is no documented compliance mismatch to score.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent, reassess compliance obligations.
IF residency or retention requirements are imposed externally, verify both agents meet them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention expectations before deployment.
Confirm no secrets are handled by either agent.
requires-engineering: add residency/retention controls if regulated data is later processed.
